The '''Sipsk'ud''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Sipsk system/Legends|Sipsk system]]<ref name="TEAOC" /><ref name="Planetnamia" /> in the [[Kanz sector/Legends|Kanz sector]].<ref name="DitSPoL" /> They were broadly [[Bird/Legends|avian]] in appearance, with a yellow [[Duck/Legends|duck]]-like beak and white feathers. They had a large cluster of seven [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] on their heads, and at least one Sipsk'ud wore a sealed spacesuit while in an atmosphere suitable for species such as [[Human/Legends|Humans]].<ref name="CSW:TEA7" />

During the [[Old Republic era]], many Sipsk'ud were converted to [[Vianism]] by [[Argazdan/Legends|Argazdan]] settlers from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="DitSPoL" /> They were one of many species that could be found wandering the streets of [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] at the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="LW">{{StoryCite|story=Lone Wolf: A Tale of Obi-Wan and Luke|book=SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story}}</ref> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a Sipsk'ud was present among the [[Spacer/Legends|space-freighters]] recruited by young [[Berd Lin]] to rescue [[Myoris Lin|his mother]] and her school after they were kidnapped by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[Stafuv Rahz]]. The individual was also present when Lin revised his plan in order to avoid an Imperial trap.<ref name="CSW:TEA7" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Spider_Duck_2.jpg|thumb|left|A Sipsk'ud]]
The Sipsk'ud were created by [[Russ Manning]] in the form of an unnamed [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] present in ''[[Bring Me the Children]]'', an arc of the [[Star Wars (comic strip)|''Star Wars'' comic strip]] published in [[1980]], and reprinted in color in [[Classic Star Wars: The Early Adventures 7|''Classic Star Wars: The Early Adventures'' 7]] in [[1995]]. The species did not receive a name at that time.

[[Adrick Tolliver]] introduced the name for the species in "[[Death in the Slave Pits of Lorrd]]," a story released on [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]]. The story did not explicitly connect the Sipsk'ud with the species seen in Manning's comic, but Tolliver noted in his endnotes for the story that "authorial intent is that they are the ducklike species with multiple eyes seen in ''Classic Star Wars: Bring Me the Children''." While he also noted that "authorial intent is, as always, to be taken with a grain of salt,"<ref name="Endnotes">{{Blog|taloncard|12|Endnotes for "Death in the Slave Pits of Lorrd"}}</ref> Keeper of the Holocron [[Leland Chee]] later indicated that the name did go with the being seen in ''Bring Me the Children'',<ref name="FB">{{Facebook|noprofile=1|author=Leland Chee|date=September 20, 2012|quote=It's fair to say this is the name.|url=permalink.php?story_fbid=455963544424577&id=201820953172172|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/FcSF2}}</ref> and [[Abel G. Peña]]'s short story "[[Lone Wolf: A Tale of Obi-Wan and Luke]]" cements this connection by referring to "spider-eyed Sipsk'ud mallards."<ref name="LW" />
